verdict.line: You lose this if you let Nasus farm Siphoning Strike stacks past level 9 untouched; you win it by using your level 3-5 stun combo to force a kill before his Fury of the Sands comes online.

brief.thesis: Nasus has no stun, no gap-closer, and no real answer to a committed all-in before level 6 — he only has single-target Siphoning Strike (Q) to poke back. Renekton's W (Ruthless Predator) stun and E (Slice and Dice) dash give him the only hard engage in the lane, which is why OP.GG grades this a lane and solo-kill edge for Renekton (48.2% over 1901 games is close to even precisely because that edge has to be converted before Nasus's Q stacks and Fury of the Sands catch up).

theirWindow.what: At 700 range, Wither slows your Movement and Attack Speed the moment he lands it on you, which kills your ability to stick with E or walk away from a bad trade. Don't commit a dash-in all-in into a fresh Wither — bait it on a minion or wait it out (15/14/13/12/11s cooldown by rank).

yourWindow.what: Once you have W (Ruthless Predator) and E (Slice and Dice) online, dash in and land the double-slash stun, then Q (Cull the Meek) and autos to build past 50 Fury. At 50+ Fury your W becomes a triple slash that strips his shields and stuns for 1.5s instead of 0.75s — chain it into a kill attempt, not just a poke.

start.why: Run with the 90.2% pick rate option — the extra sustain and early damage directly support the all-in window at levels 3-5, which is the entire point of this matchup.

boots.why: 63.8% pick rate and the right call here — Nasus's damage is almost entirely basic-attack and Siphoning Strike autos, and Steelcaps blunts both his trading pattern and his Q farm pressure if he ever auto-trades you.

core.why: The shield and burst proc reward exactly the stun-into-combo all-in you're looking for in the level 3-6 window.
Armor shred stacks with your E's own armor reduction, keeping your damage relevant into Nasus's Fury of the Sands health pool later.
This is the 20.9%-pick, 55.7%-winrate path — the damage-over-time conversion is what lets you survive Nasus's Soul Eater lifesteal and R health drain in extended trades past level 9.

runes.keystoneWhy: This is the higher-pick page (36.4% vs 10.1%) for a reason — Conqueror's stacking adaptive force and healing reward the multi-hit W/Q trades you're forcing, and it keeps paying off into the longer fights Nasus's R creates past level 6.

summoners.why: 91% of Renekton players run this combo here, and it matches the matchup's own stated solo-kill advantage — Ignite is what converts a level 3-5 stun combo into an actual kill instead of just a shove.

playing.title: All-in the moment Wither is down
playing.detail: Nasus's only peel or escape tool is Wither (W), on a 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown by rank. Track it off cooldown timing from his last cast and commit your E-dash all-in the instant it's unavailable.

playing.title: Bank Fury before you engage
playing.detail: Autos and Q (Cull the Meek) build Fury passively. Walk into range and land a few hits before you commit W, so your stun lands as the empowered 3-hit, 1.5s version instead of the weaker 0.75s one.

playing.title: Deny Siphoning Strike stacks
playing.detail: Nasus's Q (Siphoning Strike) only grows in power when it kills a minion, so every wave you shove past him or contest the last hit on is a stack he never gets. This matters more than any single trade.

playing.title: Punish his Spirit Fire commitment
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (E) is a 650-range ground zone on a 12s cooldown — once he's cast it to poke or zone you, his damage options are down for a window. Use E (Slice and Dice) to close the gap during that window.

playing.title: Time your ult to finish, not to start
playing.detail: Dominus (R) gives you bonus Health and ongoing Fury generation — pop it mid-fight once he's already committed, not as your opener, so the extra Fury lets your W stay in its empowered state for the whole trade.

playing.title: Stop dueling him alone after level 13
playing.detail: Once his Q stacks compound and his R uptime approaches permanent with CDR, a 1v1 duel stops being free. Shift to picking him off with allies or denying his split-push rather than re-testing the lane.

playing.title: Cut his sustain when behind
playing.detail: If you fall behind on kills, his Soul Eater lifesteal and R health drain will out-sustain your damage in any extended fight. Executioner's Calling directly answers this.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, and summoner spells above are pulled directly from measured win-rate and pick-rate data on the current patch — the power-curve timing and trade-pattern reasoning is tactical judgement layered on top of that data, not a separate stat.

stats.opponentTip: Apply pressure early game to prevent Nasus from farming lane and to gain lane control. Build up Fury while engaging whenever Nasus stands in range.
